activity.notes: 1759 is a source-attested REPRESENTATIVE PUBLICATION POINT for Voltaire's Candide (Candide, ou l'Optimisme), published in Geneva by Cramer, and is not his full intellectual career or a claim that Geneva was part of the Kingdom of France. The French Kingdom relation denotes his broader intellectual and political context; the publication's actual Geneva place is preserved in notes. Voltaire is the literary name of François-Marie Arouet, not a second Person.

sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France, Gallica: Les classiques du XVIIIe siècle
sources.citation_text: National Library of France identifies Voltaire as the pen name of François-Marie Arouet (1694–1778), and documents the first Candide (Geneva, Cramer, 1759).

sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France: Candide historical publication notes
sources.citation_text: BnF's annotated original shows that Candide was published in 1759, printed in Geneva and broadly circulated in France and other European countries.

spatial_disposition.evidence: Candide 1759 publication in independent Geneva established by BnF; Kingdom of France expresses French national/intellectual affiliation, NOT ownership of Geneva. Person-specific exact place and temporal place-function ID were not reviewed; do not assign an arbitrary political centroid.
